In this prospective study, AI-enhanced ECG and AI-guided focused cardiac ultrasound (AI-FoCUS) were assessed for detecting SHD (left ventricular EF < 40%, ≥moderate aortic stenosis, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, or cardiac amyloidosis) in 995 adults against comprehensive echocardiography performed within 30 min of AI-FoCUS.

title: A view-engage-predict framework for enhancing brain-behavior mapping with naturalistic movie-watching fMRI
creator: Yunrui Zhang, Emily S Finn, Mert R Sabuncu, Amy Kuceyeski
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Most brain-behavior mapping studies rely on resting-state functional connectivity (FC), but this approach has known accuracy limits and can be outperformed by movie-watching FC. Here, we present a novel deep neural network framework to predict cognitive scores and sex from FC during naturalistic movie viewing, and examine how movie content and its ability to synchronize brain activity across individuals relate to prediction performance.

title: Top developments in clinical cardiac electrophysiology–2025
creator: Brian Olshansky

title: Individualized dose–response algorithm vs weight-based heparin dosing for intraprocedural anticoagulation during atrial fibrillation ablation
creator: Jared Bryce Pleash, Jonathan O’Leary, Michael David Fryer, Tuppence Richman, Philip Cumpston, Matthew K.Y. Tung
description: BackgroundEffective anticoagulation during atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation is essential to minimize thromboembolic and bleeding complications. Conventional weight-based (WB) unfractionated heparin dosing does not account for interindividual variability in anticoagulation response and may result in suboptimal activated clotting time (ACT) control.

title: Early arrhythmia recurrence during the blanking period after pulsed-field ablation for atrial fibrillation

description: BackgroundPulmonary vein isolation is a cornerstone in the treatment of atrial fibrillation, with procedural success traditionally assessed after a 3-month “blanking period” to account for early postablation arrhythmias. title: Dynamic changes in cardiac autonomic function persist in the postacute phase after SARS-CoV-2 infection in a hamster model of COVID-19

description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). title: Nurse practitioner-led CIED monitoring during MRI in pediatric and adult patients with congenital heart disease
creator: Brynn E. Dechert, Martin J. LaPage
description: BackgroundRecent evidence shows minimal risk to patients undergoing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs), even those with MRI non-conditional devices or epicardial and/or abandoned leads.ObjectiveWe report our experience with peri-MRI device care for pediatric and adult patients with congenital heart disease (CHD) provided by pediatric electrophysiology (EP) nurse practitioner(s) (NP).

title: Air Conditioning Use and Ambulance Transports for Heat-Related Illness Across Summer Months in the Tokyo Metropolitan Area

description: Heat is a growing public health threat, yet seasonal variations in adaptation including air conditioning (AC) use remain poorly understood. We examined the modifying role of electricity consumption (EC), a proxy for air conditioning (AC) use, in the association between maximum temperature and ambulance transports for heat-related illness in the Tokyo Metropolitan Area.

description: BackgroundThis study aimed to investigate the differential expression of Musashi 2 (MSI2) in the single and double corpus lutea of Mongolian sheep (Xing’an black sheep) and its role in multiparity.ResultsResults showed two synonymous SNPs identified in the exons of MSI2. MSI2 was co-localized with GDF9/BMP15 in follicles and corpus lutea.

title: Chronic central-targeted Interleukin-6 overexpression promotes hippocampal and cortical neuropathology in the Tg2576 mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease
creator: Carla Canal, Kevin Aguilar, Gemma Comes, Elisenda Sanz, Mercedes Giralt, Paula Sanchis, Juan Hidalgo
description: BackgroundInterleukin-6 (IL-6) is a cytokine detected in the brains and peripheral fluids of both Alzheimer’s disease (AD) patients and mouse models, where its levels correlate with amyloid-beta (Aβ) burden and plaque deposition. Interestingly, IL-6 deficiency ameliorates cognitive deficits and attenuates hippocampal neuroinflammation, whereas astrocyte-targeted IL-6 signaling via its soluble receptor accentuates pathological features in AD mouse models.

title: Uni-portal thoracoscopic lymph node dissection under the left prominence: pause ventilation technique
creator: Yanhui Yang, Jinyuan Mei, Jiaxiong Luo, Linzhi Xie, Cui Ma, Ji Li, Yi Wang, Xiaoyang Xie
description: TechniqueUni-portal video-assisted thoracoscopic lobectomy (UVATS) has become a well-established technique; however, performing a complete lymphadenectomy, particularly the removal of lymph nodes located below the left hemithorax (LHLN), remains a challenging procedure. To our knowledge, there are limited reports addressing the use of pause ventilation during UVATS for LHLN dissection.

title: Printing to Fight Antimicrobial Resistance Through Nano/Microstructured Platforms
creator: Giorgia Puleo, Silvia Orecchio, Dario Savoca, Claudia Pellerito, Vittorio Ferrara, Vincenzo Piscopo, Sebastiano Alberto Fortuna, Alessandra Giardina, Bruno Pignataro, Paola Costanzo, Floriana Campanile, Giuseppe Arrabito
description: Antimicrobial resistance is one of the most pressing global public health threats, responsible for millions of deaths annually. To tackle this issue, additive manufacturing has been increasingly exploited to fabricate structured antimicrobial platforms with precise control over composition, geometry, and release kinetics.

title: GABAergic neurons in the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray mediate fentanyl withdrawal and self-administration in mice
creator: Yueyi Chen, Xi Cheng, Yue Cao, Tiange Xiao, Alexander A. Chubykin, Adam Kimbrough
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Opioid addiction is characterized by compulsive drug seeking and use, accompanied by pain and heightened pain sensitivity (hyperalgesia) during withdrawal, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood, especially for fentanyl. Using whole-brain Fos mapping and network analysis, we found that the periaqueductal gray is a central hub brain region engaged during fentanyl withdrawal, suggesting a prominent role for this region in withdrawal-associated neural signaling and warranting further examination.

title: Sexual Satisfaction and Orgasm Experiences During Partnered and Solo Sex Among 27,931 Users of the Flo App
creator: Yella Hewings-Martin, Adam C. Cunningham, Jordan Rullo, Karen L. Blair, Carley Prentice, Anna Klepchukova, Liudmila Zhaunova
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Orgasm frequency during partnered sexual activities is thought to be a predictor of sexual satisfaction. Less is known about the relationship between orgasms from solo sexual activities and satisfaction. The current study examined the interplay between orgasms and sexual satisfaction in partnered and solo contexts, the role of sexual variety, and distinct sexual activities in a sample of 27,931 Flo app users (99% female, 96% women).

title: Antiviral therapy and hidden predictors of postoperative outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma
creator: Nadeem Ashraf, Qingyong Hong, Zhidong Guo, Kun Li
description: BackgroundHepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a global health burden and hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a common cause. Antiviral therapy has the possibility to reduce the incidence of HCC, and recurrence of HCC after surgical resection.MethodsA total of 410 HCC patients had hepatectomy at Zhongnan hospital of Wuhan University.

title: Transmission and cost-effectiveness modelling to estimate the progress towards elimination and future strategy optimisation for gambiense human African trypanosomiasis in Uganda
creator: Ching-I Huang, Marina Antillon, Ronald E. Crump, Samuel A. Sutherland, Paul R. Bessell, Albert Mugenyi, Richard Selby, Paul E. Brown, Brady Hooley, Andrew Hope, Sophie Dunkley, Rob Sunnucks, Steve J. Torr, Fabrizio Tediosi, Joseph Ndung’u, Emily H. Crowley, Eric Kidega, Charles Wamboga, Kat S. Rock
description: BackgroundGambiense human African trypanosomiasis (gHAT) is a vector-borne disease with hundreds of thousands of people living at risk across Sub-Saharan Africa. Uganda, having reduced gHAT cases reported annually from 948 in 2000 to zero local cases since 2020, is a frontrunner to be verified by the World Health Organization (WHO) as having achieved elimination of transmission (EoT) of gHAT.

title: Hybrid deep learning time-to-event modeling of major adverse cardiovascular events using coronary artery calcium score scans
creator: Justin N. Kim, Juhwan Lee, Ammar Hoori, Hao Wu, Tao Hu, Sadeer Al-Kindi, Mohamed Makhlouf, Robert Gilkeson, Sanjay Rajagopalan, David L. Wilson
description: Background:The Agatston score from non-contrast coronary calcium scoring scan (CACS) is a robust predictor of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) but summarizes total calcium burden and may miss other risk-related imaging information in CACS. We hypothesized that a hybrid deep-learning (DL) model integrating image features with clinical, Agatston, and calcium-omics data could improve MACE risk prediction.

title: Combating Alzheimer’s through sleep and exercise (CASE): A study protocol
creator: Debbie Chung, Brittany A Larsen, Laurent G Garchitorena Gomez, Alberto R Ramos, Neva J Kirk-Sanchez, Girardin Jean-Louis, Azizi A Seixas
description: Dementia affects over 55 million people worldwide, with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) comprising most cases. Because curative therapies remain unavailable, there is an urgent need for prevention strategies that target modifiable risk factors. Behavioral interventions—particularly sleep improvement and physical activity—can independently benefit cognition, brain function, and cardiometabolic health, yet their combined (potentially synergistic) effects and scalable delivery models remain underexplored.

title: Voice and Speech in Deep Brain Stimulation in Dystonia: A Retrospective Study, Systematic Review, and Meta‐Analysis
creator: Ian O. Bledsoe, Nutan Sharma, Marta San Luciano, Jill L. Ostrem, Nicole E. Buie, Gaia Arno, Mikayla Day, Kristina Simonyan
description: BackgroundRelatively little is known about voice and speech abnormalities and their changes after deep brain stimulation (DBS) in patients with dystonia.ObjectiveThe aim was to determine the incidence of speech abnormalities, including laryngeal dystonia, among patients with dystonia receiving DBS and to characterize their response to this neurosurgical neuromodulation.

title: Associations Between Cumulative Head Trauma and Self‐Reported Parkinsonism and Parkinson's Disease in Former Soccer Players
creator: Annalise E. Miner, Matthew J. Kmiecik, Niharika Namburi, Nathaniel Dunckley, Charles H. Adler, Erika D. Driver‐Dunckley, Christopher J. Nowinski, Joshua Gottesman, Yorghos Tripodis, Robert A. Stern, Ann C. McKee, Thor D. Stein, Jesse Mez, Farren B.S. Briggs, Michael L. Alosco
description: BackgroundCumulative head trauma, encompassing repetitive head impacts (RHI) and traumatic brain injury (TBI), has been associated with later‐life neurodegenerative disease. Studies on parkinsonism/Parkinson's disease (PD) have evaluated RHI and TBI in isolation, yielding mixed results. Cumulative head trauma may better predict PD risk.

title: Spatiotemporal Progression Patterns of Striatal Dopamine Depletion and Cerebral Hypoperfusion in Parkinson's Disease

description: BackgroundThe identification of Parkinson's disease (PD) subtypes is crucial for predicting the disease course and designing personalized therapeutic strategies.ObjectivesThe aim of the study was to characterize the heterogeneity of the spatiotemporal evolutionary patterns of striatal dopamine depletion and cerebral hypoperfusion in PD.MethodsWe retrospectively enrolled 708 patients with newly diagnosed PD and 50 healthy controls who underwent dual‐phase 18F‐FP‐CIT PET scans.

title: An Aberrant Right Colic Artery Arising From the Right Gastroepiploic Artery

title: “If I go down, if I crumble, then everybody does” — identity crisis and emotional strain in parents of children with rare and undiagnosed conditions: a qualitative study
creator: Tara Maria Hoffmann, Bettina Friedrich, Celine Lewis
description: BackgroundCaring for a child with a rare condition can significantly impact parents’ emotional health, yet research on the emotional impact is limited. This qualitative interview study sought to investigate the lived experiences of parents who are experiencing higher psychological burden.

In this work a new family of squaramide anion transporters appended with two different lysosome targeting groups via a 1,4‐substituted benzene spacer were synthesised.

title: Perioperative severe hemorrhage in pediatric kidney transplantation: frequency, risk factors, and outcomes

description: BackgroundTo characterize severe hemorrhage and determine its frequency, risk factors, and consequences in the perioperative period of pediatric kidney transplantation.MethodsSingle-center retrospective study of children undergoing their first kidney transplant between 2008 and 2015. Severe hemorrhage was defined using a data-driven cluster analysis to identify patients with high perioperative bleeding volume and blood component requirements.

title: Utilization and outcomes of COVID-19 positive donors in pediatric kidney transplantation—a population-based study

Ardern‐Jones, Kara Heelan, Jesse P. Hirner, Ander Mayor, Mariette Labots, Markus V. Starink, Conny J. van der Laken, Vincent Si

However, data on its clinical presentation and optimal therapeutic approaches remain sparse.ObjectivesThis study aimed to further characterize the clinical features and outcomes of ICI‐EF.

description: Despite revolutionary advances in tumor immunotherapy, its efficacy is often limited by antigen heterogeneity, immune exhaustion, and impaired immune cell infiltration caused by the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). description: During frozen dough production, transportation, and processing, temperature fluctuations expose yeast to freeze-thaw (FT) stress, causing yeast cellular damage. This study investigated the effects of FT cycles on mitochondrial structure and function in yeast under different fermentation processes. As FT cycles increased, cell mortality, mitochondrial membrane potential, and superoxide anion (O2.

title: Physical Exercise as an Adjuvant to Glucocorticoid Therapy: Clinical Recommendations and Evidence Review
creator: Paula Etayo-Urtasun, Mikel L. Sáez de Asteasu, Mikel Izquierdo
description: Glucocorticoids are extensively prescribed for managing immune-mediated and inflammatory diseases. While clinically effective, prolonged glucocorticoid therapy induces adverse effects that compromise physical function and may attenuate the benefits of exercise interventions. Current exercise guidelines, however, inadequately address the complexities of concurrent glucocorticoid treatment.

title: Racism and alterations in brain structure and function: A narrative review of emerging neuroimaging evidence in racialized individuals
creator: Seyed Mohammad Mahdi Moshirian Farahi, Jude Mary Cénat
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Racial discrimination functions as a chronic psychosocial stressor that underlies racial trauma and elevates risk for mental disorders among racialized individuals. Emerging neuroimaging research has identified associations between experiences of racial discrimination and alterations in brain structure and function. However, the limited number of studies among racialized individuals constitutes a major gap in the scientific literature, leading to critical deficiencies in scientific knowledge, clinical practice, and informed public health strategies.

title: LPP slopes index attention dynamics: Evidence from mindfulness inductions
creator: Ben Swanson, Yanli Lin, Matt R Judah
description: Substantial evidence suggests that the late positive potential (LPP) indexes motivated attention to salient stimuli. title: Real-World Response and Super-Response to Eptinezumab over 48 Weeks in Migraine: The Prospective Multicenter EMBRACE III Study
creator: Piero Barbanti, Cinzia Aurilia, Massimo Filippi, Alberto Doretti, Florindo d’Onofrio, Paola Scatena, Rosario Vecchio, Roberta Messina, Luisa Vinciguerra, Angelo Ranieri, Francesco Baldisseri, Paola Torelli, Marco Russo, Carolina Cutrona, Giovanna Viticchi, Gabriella Egeo, Massimo Autunno, Francesca

title: Development of a machine learning model using systemic and ophthalmic parameters to detect sleep-disordered breathing in glaucoma patients
creator: Naoki Kiyota, Mai Yamazaki, Noriko Himori, Takahiro Ninomiya, Koki Osada, Takeshi Yabana, Shigeto Maekawa, Satoru Tsuda, Kazuko Omodaka, Yu Yokoyama, Toru Nakazawa

The placenta plays a central role in translating maternal metabolic disturbances into fetal and vascular consequences.

title: Timing and sequence between a thick fascia covering muscles and a cutaneous nerve perforating it: a study using histological sections of human fetuses
creator: Dan Guo, Dongming Xu, Zhe-Wu Jin, Feng Han, Gen Murakami, Masahito Yamamoto
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A deep fascia is believed to develop after a cutaneous nerve (CN) reaches the subcutaneous tissue. The present study aimed to examine a developmental sequence of the CN perforation of the deep fascia. We examined the occipital and posterior neck region as well as the anterior abdominal wall using histological sections from 12 human early fetuses at approximately 7–9 weeks of gestation age (GA) and 10 midterm fetuses at approximately 12–18 weeks GA.

The AAA+ ATPase VCP/p97 (valosin containing protein) is a key regulator of proteostasis by disassembling ubiquitinated substrates for degradation. VCP overexpression supports cancer cell survival and correlates with poor prognosis, promoting the development of VCP inhibitors as anti-cancer agents.

title: What Do Patient‐Reported Sleep Measures Assess? A Content Analysis
creator: Marie De Bruecker, Elke Veirman, An Mariman, Dirk A. Pevernagie, Katrien B. C. Hertegonne, Fré A. Bauters, Dimitri M. L. Van Ryckeghem, Geert Crombez

A literature search identified 27 PRSMs applicable across multiple sleep disorders. Meaningful concepts within items of these PRSMs were linked to ICF categories using standardised linking rules.

This study characterized and compared the physiological and sleep profiles of insomnia, OSA and COMISA in population‐based datasets from Portugal (n = 147) and Spain (n = 264), excluding patients with cardiovascular disease.

title: Persistent Sleep Disturbance Following Pandemic Lockdowns: Longitudinal Findings From the UK COVID‐19 Symptom Study Biobank
creator: Barbara Toson, Nathan J. Cheetham, Julia R. B. Brown, Carole H. Sudre, Simon Proctor, Vicky Bowyer, Nicholas R. Harvey, Desaline Joseph, COVID Symptom Study Biobank Consortium, Adam Birdseye, Claire J. Steves, Sutapa Mukherjee, Emma L. Duncan

Validated questionnaires assessing sleep disturbances, fatigue, depression, and anxiety were administered to COVID Symptom Study Biobank participants at two time periods—Autumn 2021 and Spring 2022 equinoxes—corresponding to lockdown and lifting of restrictions, respectively.

creator: Jerusa Jobim Jardim, Heraldo Luis Dias da Silveira, Nádia Assein Arús, Priscila Fernanda da Silveira Tiescher, Deise Ponzoni, Mariana Boessio Vizzotto

The objective of this systematic review was to organise this knowledge, investigating the relationship between biodiversity in urban green spaces and health outcomes in adults.

creator: Benjamin Torner, Simon Klocker, Niccolò Crescenti, Aldo J. Suria, Harald Reithofer, Michael Hübler, Daniel Zimpfer, Marcus Granegger

title: Cadaveric investigation of an ultrasound-guided obturator canal approach for obturator nerve block
creator: Takayuki Yoshida, Chutikant Vichainarong, Yousuke Nakano, Masaaki Kitada, Tatsuo Nakamoto
description: t the subpectineal plane has been reported to spread retrogradely to the obturator canal [1]. This has led to the assumption that a single subpectineal injection may be sufficient to achieve blockade of all obturator nerve fibers, regardless of their site of division.

title: 3D Printable and Electrically Conductive Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogel for Cardiac and Vascular Tissue Engineering Applications
creator: Britanny L. Stark, Jose L. Perez, Edgar A. Borrego, Wilson Poon, Sylvia L. Natividad-Diaz
description: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide. After acute myocardial infarction (AMI), the adult human heart has very limited regenerative capacities, and the electrical propagation of the myocardium is severely disrupted, which makes the patient more susceptible to heart failure and death.

title: Prevalence and socio-demographic factors associated with undernutrition among HIV-positive women of reproductive age in Mahama refugee camp, Rwanda
creator: Ben Sindayigaya, Hubert Shema, Emmanuel Niyogere, Kenny Ntwali, Nwanna Uchechukwu Kevin
description: BackgroundDespite the distribution of food rations, the existence of feeding programs, and the provision of free medical care, malnutrition and morbidity continue to pose a threat to women and children, who are the most nutritionally susceptible groups, especially during emergencies. When people consume less energy and nutrients than they require to maintain their health, it is called undernutrition.

title: Secondhand smoke exposure at home and its association with tobacco use among adolescents in Saudi Arabia: findings from the 2022 global youth tobacco survey
creator: Moroj A Aldarmasi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSecondhand smoke (SHS) remains a preventable public health hazard that disproportionately affects adolescents. Despite the implementation of tobacco control measures in Saudi Arabia, SHS exposure within homes persists. This study assessed the prevalence of household SHS exposure among adolescents and examined its association with current tobacco/nicotine product use behaviors, including cigarettes, shisha, and e-cigarettes, using nationally representative data from the 2022 Global Youth Tobacco Survey (GYTS).MethodsA secondary analysis was conducted on the 2022 GYTS dataset for Saudi Arabia, comprising 6,983 students aged

title: The Covid-19 pandemic as an inflection point in US mortality trends from hematologic and circulatory system diseases: a piecewise trend analysis
creator: Amirali Koohi Bachemir, Zhenshan Sun, Melika Safari, Nasrin Borumandnia, Hamid Alavi Majd
description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare systems and may have influenced mortality trends in hematologic-immune disorders (D50-D89) and Diseases of the circulatory system (I00-I99). This study evaluates US mortality trends from 2010 to 2023 to assess potential pandemic-related changes.MethodsWe utilized spline regression modeling on CDC WONDER mortality data (2010–2023) to quantify post-pandemic trend shifts in both age-adjusted and sex/age-stratified mortality rates.

title: The impact of mHealth interventions on health-promoting behaviors in pregnant women: a randomized clinical trial
creator: Fateme Asadollahi, Samira Ebrahimzadeh Zagami, Robab Latifnejad Roudsari
description: BackgroundHealth-promoting behaviors are crucial for maternal and fetal well-being during pregnancy, yet many women face barriers to adopting these practices. Mobile health technologies offer innovative solutions by providing personalized interventions. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a comprehensive mHealth application in promoting health behaviors among pregnant women.

title: Factors associated with preference for in-person versus remote consultations in inflammatory bowel disease in the United Kingdom: secondary analysis of an online survey
creator: Keith Bodger, Frederick Taylor, Pratik Rai, Liz Dobson, Judith Bunn, Stephen Grainger, Fraser Cummings, Stuart Bloom, Nicholas Kennedy
description: IntroductionThe coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic accelerated use of remote consultations as an alternative to in-person inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) care. However, factors associated with preference for remote or in-person follow-up remain poorly understood.MethodsWe undertook a retrospective analysis of an electronic follow-up survey completed by patients who had previously used an online IBD self-assessment tool during the early pandemic.

title: MASLD, diabetes and PMOS across the female life stages
creator: Elisabet Stener-Victorin, Sofia Carlsson, Hannes Hagström, Nayere Taebnia
description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and type 2 diabetes, which affect approximately 38% and 10.5%, respectively, of adults globally, intersect critically in women through polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), previously known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent but under-recognised cardiometabolic disorder affecting 10–13% of reproductive-age women.

title: Genetics of MASLD: a diabetes perspective
creator: Josh Bilson, Hanieh Yaghootkar
description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent in people with type 2 diabetes and represents a major contributor to liver-related and extrahepatic morbidity and mortality. Despite this strong epidemiological overlap, the clinical course of MASLD in diabetes is highly heterogeneous and not fully explained by conventional metabolic risk factors.

title: Estimating Adult and Old Age Mortality From Parental Survival Histories Collected Over the Phone: A Validation Study From Bangladesh
creator: Md Tazvir Amin, Md Mahabubur Rahman, M Moinuddin Haider, Nurul Alam, Georges Reniers, Stephane Helleringer
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesBangladesh, a lower‐middle‐income (LMIC) South Asian country, relies on survey data for measuring adult mortality. Mobile phone surveys are an appealing alternative to in‐person surveys because they are cheaper and can be deployed when enumerator mobility is hindered. In this contribution, we examined the quality of ‘Parental Survival History’ data collected over the phone by comparing it with data from a Health and Demographic Surveillance System.MethodsWe conducted a mobile phone survey from July to December 2021 among residents of the Matlab HDSS.

title: Molecular and physiological characterization of two sunflower near-isogenic lines with contrasting haplotypes for leaf senescence
creator: Marco Moroldo, Nicolas Blanchet, Nicolas Pouilly, Stéphanie Pateyron, Marie-Laure Martin, Etienne Delannoy, Cédric Cassan, Yves Gibon, Sébastien Carrère, Guillaume Marti, Nicolas Bernard Langlade
description: BackgroundLeaf senescence is regulated by several genetic mechanisms and environmental factors. During senescence, cellular organelles are degraded and chlorophylls are lost. Concomitantly, macromolecules are broken down into smaller molecules that are transported into tissues like seeds, a process called nutrient remobilization. By reducing photosynthesis and increasing nutrient remobilization, senescence affects seed yield and seed protein.

title: Association of the CHG Index with the onset, progression, and prognosis of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: findings from two large prospective cohorts
creator: Zehao Zhao, Yingxun Bai, Changsheng Ma, Tianyi Wang, Libo Zhao, Xiliang Zhao, Quan Li, Yaodong Ding, Yang Zhang, Li Lin, Wenjie Wang, Jiayi Han, Yong Zeng
description: BackgroundCardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents a composite disease state driven by glucose and lipid metabolic dysregulation. The Cholesterol, High-density lipoprotein, and Glucose (CHG) index reflects the composite burden of these metabolic factors. However, its impact on the onset, stage-wise progression, and prognosis of CKM syndrome remains unclear.MethodsThis study utilized data from two large-scale prospective cohorts.

title: Exploring General Practice Nurses' Experiences of an Intervention to Support Social Connectedness Among Older Adults: A Qualitative Descriptive Study
creator: Cristina Thompson, Kath Peters, Amy Montgomery, Elizabeth Halcomb
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimThis paper explores the experience of general practice nurses implementing a nurse‐led social prescribing intervention to improve older people's social connectedness.DesignQualitative descriptive study within a multi‐phase mixed methods project.MethodsEight Australian general practice nurses working in a health connector role participated in semi‐structured interviews at implementation‐end (n = 8) and 12 months later (n = 5), and two focus groups, held during implementation. Interviews addressed participants' reasons for engaging in the intervention, perceptions of training, the experience of intervention delivery and sustainability.

title: Parents' Experiences of Patient Safety Incidents During Their Child's Hospitalization: A Qualitative Study
creator: Mi Young Kim, Yujeong Kim
description: AimsPatient safety incidents involving hospitalized children can have significant impacts on both patients and their families. However, previous research has primarily focused on healthcare professionals' perspectives, and studies exploring parents' experiences of patient safety incidents in paediatric settings remain limited. This study aimed to identify parents' experiences of patient safety incidents during their child's hospitalization.DesignQualitative study.

title: AOSNP‐ADAPTR resource level‐based recommendations on practical diagnostic strategies for ependymomas
creator: Laveniya Satgunaseelan, Michael E Buckland, Geeta Chacko, Kenta Masui, Junji Shibahara, Vani Santosh, Maysa Al‐Hussaini, Sung‐Hye Park, Tarik Tihan, Ho‐Keung Ng, Pieter Wesseling, David N Louis, Chitra Sarkar, Takashi Komori
description: Ependymomas are uncommon primary tumors of the central nervous system (CNS) that affect both children and adults. In recent years, molecular analyses have identified multiple subtypes of ependymal tumors based on location, patterns of CpG island methylation, and gene fusion events.

title: Comments to the “Letter to the Editor” for the manuscript titled “Increased expression of inflammasome signaling genes and proteins in selective brain regions in the intermediate stage of Alzheimer's disease”
creator: Juan Pablo de Rivero Vaccari, David A Davis, Andrew P Sawaya, Susanna P Garamszegi, Xiaoyan Sun, Ayled Barreda, Helen M Bramlett, Sakir Humayun Gultekin, W Dalton Dietrich, Robert W Keane, Regina T Vontell
description: Beta amyloid diffuse plaques, neurofibrillary tangles and neuritic plaques, are increased in densities at the intermediate stage of Alzheimer's neuropathological change. These pathological changes releasing Pathogen‐Associated Molecular Patterns (PAMPs) and Damage‐Associated Molecular Patterns (DAMPs). These molecules are sensed by pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) and trigger intracellular responses.

title: Dysregulated TIE‐2 expression is associated with blood‐brain barrier leakiness and Alzheimer's disease‐related neuropathology
creator: Selvi Ince, Carol Van Hulle, Gwendlyn Kollmorgen, Clara Quijano‐Rubio, Carey Gleason, Barbara B Bendlin, Ozioma Okonkwo, Sanjay Asthana, Kaj Blennow, Henrik Zetterberg, Sterling C Johnson, Seth Love, J Scott Miners
description: Cerebral hypoperfusion and blood–brain barrier (BBB) leakiness are related to cognitive decline and the onset and spread of Aβ and tau pathology in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Disrupted angiopoietin/TIE (ANGPT/TIE) signalling causes neurovascular instability and BBB leakiness accelerating cognitive decline and disease pathology in mouse models of AD.

title: Effectiveness of a behavioral weight management intervention by race, ethnicity, income, and education: a meta-analysis
creator: Lorraine T. Dean, Shadiya L. Moss, Gary D. Foster, Alexandra M. Lee, John W. Apolzan, Amy A. Gorin, Stanley Heshka, John M. Jakicic, David G. Marrero, Patrick M. O’Neil, Sherry L. Pagoto, Ana M. Palacios, Kelly N. B. Palmer, Renee J. Rogers, Deborah F. Tate, Stephanie L. Fitzpatrick, Michelle I. Car
description: BackgroundRacially and ethnically marginalized groups experience disproportionately high obesity rates, but are underrepresented in clinical trials of obesity treatments. Obesity treatments seem less effective for marginalized groups, but studies are characterized by small samples, clinic-based treatments, and little attention to socioeconomic position.

title: Antimicrobial resistance among clinical isolates associated with combat-related infections in Ukraine: first nationwide surveillance, 2023-2024
creator: Ludmila Kasatkina, Ihnat Havrylov, Anzhela Sboieva, Valentyna Yanovska, Tetiana Glushkevych, Artem Horbachevskyi
description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a critical global health threat, which reduces the effectiveness of treatment and drives higher morbidity, mortality, and costs. In Ukraine, the problem has been further aggravated by Russia’s full-scale invasion, with favorable conditions for the spread of resistant pathogens.

title: National genomic surveillance reveals global plasmid and chromosomal dissemination routes of blaNDM-1
creator: Ricardo Gutiérrez, Manuel Ramírez-Cardoce, Tábata Elizondo-Alvarez, Francisco Duarte-Martínez, Estela Cordero-Laurent, Elvira Segura-Retana, Daniel Cascante-Serrano, Romein Walters-Mais, Cristian Pérez-Corrales, Cristina García-Marín, Heylin Estrada-Murillo, Ernesto Amuy-Morera, Ruth Arce-Bejarano,
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The global spread of New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase (NDM)–producing Gram-negative bacteria poses a major threat to healthcare systems worldwide, yet the processes driving their long-term establishment at national scales remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate a decade of nationwide surveillance with high-resolution genomics to reconstruct the emergence, dissemination, and evolution of blaNDM in Costa Rica, from its first detection in 2014 to a major hospital outbreak during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Epigenetic insights into cancer metastasis via lineage trans-differentiation
creator: Cong Zou, Caixia Xia, Hongwei Peng, Shenjuan Li, Jia Shang, Wan Xiang, Haoli Ma, Fangjin Chen, Xinyue Cao, Gang Wang
description: t profoundly divergent transcriptional and phenotypic profiles.1 This genomic-phenotypic dissociation strongly implicates nongenetic, epigenetically mediated mechanisms as principal determinants of metastatic competence. The cancer epigenome, long recognized as a domain of therapeutic opportunity,2 has until recently lacked a coherent mechanistic framework connecting its dysregulation to the generation of metastasis-competent clones (see Fig. 1).

title: Retention in care among women with HIV: A systematic review of treatment continuity during pregnancy and postpartum
creator: Stine Hansen, Klara Tetzschner Madsen, Nina Weis, Ellen Moseholm
description: IntroductionPregnant women with HIV are at risk of reduced engagement in HIV care during pregnancy and postpartum. Retention in care, defined as continuous engagement in HIV‐related treatment and follow‐up, is essential to achieve virological suppression and prevent vertical transmission. Contemporary evidence on retention in care during pregnancy and postpartum among women with HIV in high‐income countries remains limited.

title: Novel markers on microvascular flow imaging for identifying holoprosencephaly
creator: Zhen Li, Yuanjie Cui, Cuixia Guo, Juan Zhang, Lei Wang, Zhaoxia JIA, Yuting Wu, Qingqing Wu, Lijuan Sun
description: ObjectivesTo establish gestational age-specific reference ranges for two new indices, the forehead-anterior cerebral artery angle (FACAA) and forehead-anterior cerebral artery distance (FACAD), and to objectively evaluate their diagnostic effectiveness, measured using Doppler technology with microvascular flow imaging, for identifying holoprosencephaly, even the semilobar and lobar types, in early pregnancy.

title: Agatston-2.0: A next-generation AI-based coronary calcium quantification approach to improve risk stratification among individuals with zero Agatston scores – Part I
creator: Morteza Naghavi, Amir Azimi, Kyle Atlas, Anthony P Reeves, Chenyu Zhang, Seyed Reza Mirjalili, Mohammadhossein Mozafarybazargany, Amir Ghaffari Jolfayi, Ali Hashemi, Thomas Atlas, Jakob Wasserthal, Rozemarijn Vliegenthart, Claudia I Henschke, David F Yankelevitz, Andrea D Branch, Sion K Roy, Jamal S
description: BackgroundA coronary artery calcium (CAC) score of zero using the conventional Agatston scoring method (Agatston-1.0) is associated with very low cardiovascular risk (the “Power of Zero”); however, a small proportion of individuals with CAC=0 still develop coronary heart disease (CHD). Agatston-1.0 relies on thick slices (2.

title: Incretin therapy prescription in a high cardiovascular risk population: Insights from a cardiology-based cardiometabolic program
creator: Arpan Patel, Lakshya Trivedi, Rachna Prasad, Eleanora Avennati, Steven Alexander, Vu Nguyen, Thomas Kurian, Priyanka Satish
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ist, including their perception as diabetes specific medications, inadequate insurance coverage, medication costs and concern for side effects [1] Hence, there are limited real-world data into how cardiometabolic programs integrate into routine cardiology practice. In the present study, we sought to evaluate [1]: weight loss outcomes in patients prescribed incretin therapy within this program [2] adherence and safety outcomes [[3], [5]]; effects on secondary cardiometabolic outcomes, from a multidisciplinary program integrated within cardiology.

title: Developing the parenting concerns scale for cancer survivors and assessment of its validity and reliability in China
creator: Mengyao Zhou, Zifang Jiang, Liangjie Yang, Jiaxin Zhang
description: BackgroundParenting concerns impose a substantial psychological burden on cancer survivors, who must cope not only with concerns related to disease treatment but also with worries about the healthy development of their minor children. However, the early identification and assessment of this complex psychological burden remain insufficiently addressed owing to the lack of a valid and reliable assessment instrument.

title: Developmental and functional landscape of theca cells in ovarian biology
creator: Mahnaz Haddadi, Samane Adib, Christiani A. Amorim, Azam Dalman, Mojtaba Rezazadeh Valojerdi
description: Ovarian theca cells constitute essential components of the follicular microenvironment and play central roles in follicular development, steroidogenesis, and endocrine regulation. Despite their significance, the developmental origins, differentiation processes, and functional dynamics of theca cells remain incompletely defined, particularly in humans.

title: Longitudinal associations between exercise duration and sleep quality and poor sleep outcomes among college students: a latent growth curve modeling study
creator: Qian Zhang, Ruichen Sun, Hanqing Zhao, Jiakun Lyu
description: BackgroundTo investigate the effects of regular exercise on sleep quality and poor sleep outcomes, including bedtime procrastination, insomnia, and daytime sleepiness, among college students, and to examine the dynamic relationships between these outcomes and cumulative exercise duration over time.MethodsA total of 687 college students were followed longitudinally at baseline and at 4 and 8 weeks after the intervention.

title: Center of mass feedback for joint torque control during perturbed standing: a potential generalizable control approach for balance augmentation in wearable robots
creator: Kristen L. Jakubowski, Gregory S. Sawicki, Lena H. Ting
description: BackgroundExoskeletons have the potential to augment balance and decrease fall risk. However, existing balance-augmenting wearable robotic controllers have only been tested in single planes of motion during either standing or walking. Thus, it is unclear whether a single control scheme can generalize across perturbations with varying spatial properties or from standing to walking.

title: Mapping Clinical Intent in Internet Hospitals: Identifying and Profiling Patient Demand via Natural Language Processing
creator: Ruoxin Xu, Jing Liu, Huizi Ye, Tingting Yang, Kuanlie Jiang, Xiaojiao Zhu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Patient-generated text in internet hospitals represents a massive but unstructured source of clinical demand. Misalignment between rigid administrative menus and actual patient intent leads to triage inefficiency and resource mismatches. We developed a hybrid artificial intelligence framework to decode patient needs and optimize service allocation using real-world data from a tertiary internet hospital, with external validation on an independent multihospital dataset (N = 497).

title: Cardiac microcurrent therapy in heart failure: Mechanistic rationale, early clinical evidence, and future directions
creator: Marat Fudim, Faouzi Kallel, Jesus E Eduardo Rame, Javed Butler, Jeroen J Bax, Stavros G Drakos, David E Lanfear, Daniel Burkhoff, Dipthi Bachamanda Somesh, Marija Zdravkovic, Tamara Kovačević Preradović, Milosav Tomovic, Dragana Kosevic, William T Abraham, Stefan D Anker
description: Despite major advances in guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), many patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) remain symptomatic, with persistent limitations in functional capacity and health status, underscoring the need for adjunctive therapeutic strategies. Direct cardiac microcurrent (C-MIC) therapy is a non-excitatory bioelectrical intervention device to modulate myocardial remodeling rather than rhythm or acute contractility.

title: Proximity Contacts and Self-perceived Vulnerability to Diseases Among High School Students – A Preliminary Study
creator: Piotr Fedurek, Dariusz P. Danel
description: In recent years there has been much research regarding the extent to which behavioural immune system (BIS; behavioural responses that evolved to detect and avoid pathogens) is related to a variation in social profile and personality traits such as extroversion among individuals.

title: Different regulatory mechanisms of hepatitis B- and C-positive hepatocellular carcinoma by single-cell RNA sequencing
creator: Su-Jin Baek, Seung-Jin Park, Minho Lee, Won Park, Jong-Hwan Kim, Youngjin Shin, Ok-Hee Kim, Ho Joong Choi, Say-June Kim, Yeun-Jun Chung, Seon-Young Kim
description: epatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections, which together are responsible for approximately 80% of global cases.1,2 HBV, a DNA virus, and HCV, an RNA virus, possess fundamentally different genomic structures and replication strategies. This suggests they may trigger carcinogenesis through distinct molecular pathways. However, virus-specific molecular distinctions in HCC pathogenesis remain poorly defined.

title: Infectious complications of dental procedures in dogs and cats, and the impact of antimicrobial prophylaxis: a systematic review
creator: J. S. Weese, M. Soltero‐Rivera, H. E. Weese, K. Scahill
description: ObjectivesTo identify and describe available evidence pertaining to the local and systemic infectious complications in dogs and cats that have undergone dental procedures and the impact of peri‐procedural antimicrobial prophylaxis.Materials and MethodsA systematic review was performed based on Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and MetaAnalysis guidelines.

title: Silicone oil tamponade in vitreoretinal surgery and future perspective: a narrative review
creator: Cesare Mariotti, Alessio Muzi, Giulia Gregori, Oscar Matteo Gagliardi, Danilo Iannetta, Veronica Mogetta, Alberto Quarta, Maria Ludovica Ruggeri, Lorenzo Mangoni, Clara Rizzo, Rodolfo Mastropasqua, Marco Lupidi
description: PurposeSilicone oil (SO) represents an essential ocular tamponade in complex vitreoretinal surgery, due to its transparency, chemical inertness, and long-term stability. This review aims to describe the current role of SO in vitreoretinal surgery, highlighting its indications, physicochemical characteristics, and the spectrum of associated complications.

title: Chromovitrectomy: current evidence, emerging technologies, and practical applications in vitreoretinal surgery
creator: Federico Giannuzzi, Lorenzo Hu, Mattia Cusato, Matteo Mario Carlà, Emanuele Crincoli, Federico Maragno, Valentina Cestrone, Umberto De Vico, Stanislao Rizzo
description: Chromovitrectomy has revolutionized vitreoretinal surgery by enabling the visualization of nearly transparent intraocular structures. This review evaluates the clinical utility of key vital dyes, such as brilliant blue G, trypan blue, indocyanine green, and triamcinolone acetonide, focusing on their physicochemical properties, staining affinities, and safety profiles.

title: Clinical symptoms and cognitive functioning following adjunctive N-acetylcysteine in obsessive-compulsive disorder: a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
creator: Sanaz Askari, Shayan Eghdami, Mahla Tavasoli, Seyed Vahid Shariat, Masoomeh Yarahmadi, Atefeh Ghanbari Jolfaei, Elham Shirazi, Soode Tajik Esmaeeli, Mohammadreza Shalbafan
description: BackgroundObsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) often remains partially responsive to first-line treatments such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRI). N-acetylcysteine (NAC), a glutamate-modulating antioxidant, has shown promise as an adjunctive therapy, but prior studies frequently lacked standardized pharmacotherapy and cognitive outcome measures, particularly in Iranian populations.

title: Prognostic data extraction harnessing a privacy-preserving large language model: a clinician-AI collaborative retrospective evaluation in head and neck oncology
creator: Yujing Zou, Laya Rafiee Sevyeri, Farhood Farahnak, George Shenouda, Marie Duclos, Tomás Yokoo Teodoro de Souza, Khalil Sultanem, Parsa Bagherzadeh, Farhad Maleki, Shirin A. Enger
description: Privacy regulations and limited expert-validation constrain the deployment of large language models (LLMs) for electronic health record structuring. We evaluated locally deployed LLMs to extract 30 prognostic variables from 1,360 head and neck cancer reports (882 patients) using zero-shot prompting.

title: Vision transformer autoencoders captures local and non-local features in brain imaging to reveal novel genetic associations
creator: Samia R Islam, Tian Xia, Wei He, Ziqian Xie, Degui Zhi
description: Linking genetic variation to human brain structure is a key step toward understanding the biological basis of cognition and disease. Progress in this area, however, has been limited by a major challenge: imaging features are often predefined, restricting the discovery of novel associations.

title: The effect of rocking speed and cell inoculation density on hepatic spheroid size: A simple method for size modulation
creator: Michael G. Megaly, Diane Tobolt, Anthony An‐Fa Dahm Chen, Bat‐Erdene Namsrai, Benjamin Fisher, Joseph Sushil Rao, Srivasupradha Ramesh, Anudari Chimedtseren, Scott L. Nyberg, Mark Clemens, Charles Y. Lee, John C. Bischof, Erik B. Finger
description: Hepatic spheroids are widely used in bioartificial liver (BAL) systems, hepatotoxicology, and pharmacology due to improved functional stability compared with monolayer cultures. However, many existing methods rely on specialized equipment or static platforms that limit scalability and dynamic culture applications. Primary rat hepatocytes were cultured as three‐dimensional spheroids using a rocker‐based suspension system.

title: UBA1 drives cell cycle to promote malignancy and serves as a therapeutic target in Ewing Sarcoma
creator: Shangjiang Yu, Runyi Jiang, Lei Zhou, Anshun Wu, Haifeng Wei, Shaohui He, Jianru Xiao
description: BackgroundEwing sarcoma (ES) is an aggressive malignancy with high metastatic potential and poor prognosis, necessitating novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This study investigates the role of the ubiquitin-activating enzyme E1 (UBA1) in ES pathogenesis and its clinical relevance.MethodsBioinformatic analysis of GEO datasets was performed.

title: Intersection of gender and race/skin color and food consumption of adolescents: analysis of Brazil’s National Student Health Survey (PENSE) 2019
creator: Thays Maria Sant’Anna Rosa, Francine Silva dos Santos, Daniela Silva Canella
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundFood consumption of adolescents is characterized by a highly prevalent intake of ultra-processed food and a low intake of fresh or minimally processed foods. Factors such as income, gender, race/skin color, and their intersection can influence this consumption. The objective of this study was to analyze the relationship between food consumption and intersections of race/skin color and gender among Brazilian adolescents.MethodsData from Brazil’s National Student Health Survey of 2019 was used.

title: Decoverslipping of Archival Cytology Aspirate Smears for Ancillary Studies: A Review of Methods and Institutional Experience With Freezer‐Based Techniques
creator: Nyein Nyein Htun, Sinchita Roy‐Chowdhuri, Benjamin B. Morris, Gloria Hopkins Sura
description: IntroductionArchival cytology aspirate smears are increasingly used for ancillary testing, yet decoverslipping remains a practical bottleneck. This study reviews published decoverslipping methodologies and evaluates freezer‐based strategies for aspirate smears.MethodsPublished decoverslipping techniques were reviewed and compared with respect to turnaround time, tissue preservation, safety and suitability for downstream applications.

title: Converging on control: Rethinking treatment-resistant depression through network neuroscience
creator: Yoshihiro Noda

title: Ultrasound Characteristics of Twisted Pedunculated Subserosal Uterine Leiomyomas: A Case Report and a Systematic Review of the Literature
creator: Maddalena Paoli, Pietro Pasquini, Alessandra Pennetta, Ghizzi Chiara, Maria Cristina Scifo, Evaldo Giacomucci
description: Torsion of pedunculated subserosal uterine leiomyomas (TPSUL) is a rare but potentially severe condition that may require emergency surgery. This article aims to summarize the existing literature by presenting a systematic review and an illustrative case report. A total of 38 articles describing 42 cases of TPSUL were analyzed to identify recurring ultrasound features that may aid in preoperative diagnosis.

title: Temporal Trends in Decisions to Forgo KRT
creator: Susan P.Y. Wong, Lindsey M. Kornowske, Cami R. Jones, Christina L. Reynolds, Ryan Laundry, Kenn B. Daratha, Katherine R. Tuttle
description: Visual Abstract Introduction The United States National Kidney Registry indicates that, after decades of rise, the incidence rate of patients starting maintenance dialysis has been decreasing.1 This decline in the incidence rate of dialysis has been greatest among adults aged 75 years or older in whom the benefits of dialysis toward prolonging life and maintaining function are most controversial.

title: Transarterial Embolization Alone Versus Drug-Eluting Microspheres Chemoembolization for Hepatocellular Carcinoma (RAD-18-TAcE): A Multicenter Randomized Clinical Trial
creator: Cristina Mosconi, Makoto Taninokuchi Tomassoni, Sara Zanella, Alexandro Paccapelo, Giovanni Marasco, Simone Gusmini, Francesca Ratti, Diego Palumbo, Sandro Sironi, Riccardo Muglia, Marco Mario Edgardo Fronda, Marco Calandri, Paolo Fonio, Paolo Marra, Andrea Doriguzzi Breatta, Alessandro Cucchetti, F
description: PurposeTo compare transarterial embolization (TAE) and drug-eluting microspheres transarterial chemoembolization (DEM-TACE) in the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through a non-inferiority randomized clinical trial.Materials and MethodsPatients diagnosed with unresectable HCC were randomly assigned to either the TAE or DEM-TACE group.

title: Targeting Spinal Dorsal Horn Sensitisation in Chronic Pain: Mechanisms and Translational Strategies
creator: Volodymyr Krotov, Olga Kopach
description: Chronic pain is a multidimensional, highly debilitating disease arising from diverse functional and structural impairments across the nervous system. Despite heterogeneous aetiologies, chronic pain states converge on shared pathophysiological mechanisms: peripheral and central sensitisation. These dysfunctions reflect long-term functional and structural plasticity within the peripheral and central nociceptive pathways, resulting in amplified signal transmission and pain chronification.

title: Smartphone-Measured Sleep Health Risk Factors Detect Suicidal Thoughts and Behaviors Among Adolescents
creator: Jaclyn S Kirshenbaum, David Pagliaccio, Esha Trivedi, Hanga Galfalvy, Karla J Joyce, Katherine Durham, Giovanna Porta, Paul A Bloom, Trinity C Tse, Ashley Blanchard, Lauren S Chernick, Ryann N Crowley, Peter S Dayan, Lauren E Kahn, Jamie Zelazny, David A Brent, Nicholas B Allen, Randy P Auerbach
description: ObjectiveSuicide deaths and poor sleep health in adolescents have significantly increased. Smartphone sensors (eg, accelerometry) provide an unobtrusive and scalable way to monitor sleep health over extended time periods. We hypothesized that poor weekly sleep health (ie, shorter and variable time in bed; late and variable bedtime) assessed through smartphone sensors would associate with weekly suicidal thoughts and behaviors (STB).

title: Vertigo-unsolved Mystery (Meniere’s Disease) Care Redefined: Insights from a Tertiary Care Center
creator: Arti Rajpoot, Rajat Jain, Sunil Kumar, Abhishek Bahadur Singh, Veerendra Verma, Manish Chandra, Anupam Mishra
description: Background:Meniere’s disease remains a poorly understood inner ear disorder since its first description by Prosper Meniere in the early 1800s. Characterized by episodic vertigo, fluctuating hearing loss, and tinnitus, it continues to challenge clinicians due to its unpredictable course and variable treatment response. Lifestyle modification alone often fails to adequately control vertigo episodes.

title: A multiparty homomorphic encryption approach to confidential federated Kaplan–Meier survival analysis
creator: Narasimha Raghavan Veeraragavan, Svetlana Boudko, Jan Franz Nygård
description: The proliferation of real-world health data enables multi-institutional survival studies, yet privacy constraints preclude centralizing sensitive records. We present a privacy-preserving federated Kaplan–Meier framework based on threshold CKKS (Cheon-Kim-Kim-Song) homomorphic encryption that supports approximate floating-point computation and encrypted aggregation of per-time-point counts while exposing only public outputs.

title: Wahrgenommene Autonomie bei Prostatakarzinom-Langzeitüberlebenden
creator: Cornelia Peter, Ann-Kathrin Christmann, Lilly J. Schmalbrock, Stefan Schiele, Jürgen E. Gschwend, Andreas Dinkel, Kathleen Herkommer
description: HintergrundAutonomie ist ein zentrales psychologisches Bedürfnis im höheren Lebensalter und eng mit Lebensqualität, Wohlbefinden sowie funktioneller Leistungsfähigkeit verbunden. Bei Langzeitüberlebenden eines Prostatakarzinoms (PCa) kann das Autonomieerleben durch altersassoziierte Einschränkungen und therapiebedingte Belastungen beeinträchtigt sein.FragestellungErfassung der wahrgenommenen Autonomie bei PCa-Langzeitüberlebenden und Analyse soziodemographischer, klinischer und psychosozialer Einflussfaktoren.Material und MethodeQuerschnittanalyse im Rahmen des deutschen Forschungsprojekts „Familiäres Prostatakarzinom“.

title: Doege–Potter syndrome caused by a solitary fibrous tumor arising from the greater omentum: a case report
creator: Tomoki Takizawa, Tatsuya Shonaka, Chikayoshi Tani, Hiroya Kitsunai, Hiroshi Nomoto, Mototsugu Nagao, Izumi Fukuda, Yuki Kamikokura, Mishie Tanino, Hideki Yokoo
description: Doege–Potter syndrome is a rare paraneoplastic syndrome characterized by non-islet cell tumor hypoglycemia (NICTH) caused by the excessive production of insulin-like growth factor-II (IGF-II), which occurs in less than 5% of solitary fibrous tumors (SFT). SFTs most commonly arise from the pleura, whereas primary omental origins are exceedingly rare.

title: Exploratory associations between co-occurring opioid and alcohol use disorders and GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment
creator: Fares Qeadan, Ashlie McCunn, Benjamin Tingey, Philip J Kroth
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCo-occurring opioid and alcohol use disorders (OUD + AUD) are associated with morbidity, yet medications for these disorders remain underused. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor agonists (RA), prescribed for metabolic disease, may influence substance-related outcomes.

title: Does Testosterone Therapy Increase Risk of Atrial Fibrillation? Appraisal of the Contemporary Scientific and Clinical Evidence
creator: Abdulmaged M Traish, Karim Sultan Haider, Farid Saad
description: Here we review the evidence whether “testosterone” (T) therapy in hypogonadal men contributes to onset and increases the incidence of atrial fibrillation (AF). A MEDLINE review of the literature was performed, and relevant studies were analyzed and discussed. The effect of T therapy (TTh) on the incidence of AF is a controversial clinical issue that remains hotly debated.

title: Reactive airways dysfunction syndrome following acute lithium hydroxide dust exposure at a battery material production plant: a case series of 16 workers
creator: Chul Gab Lee, Soo Hyeong Park, Jeong Joon Park, Han Soo Song, Hyeon Kyeong Ko, Sung Ho Yoon
description: BackgroundReactive airways dysfunction syndrome (RADS) is an acute-onset form of irritant-induced asthma that occurs after a single high-concentration exposure to irritants. Although RADS has been documented for chlorine, ammonia, and acid fumes, no published case series has attributed RADS to lithium hydroxide (LiOH) dust inhalation.

title: Penny for your thoughts: A review and proposed model of socioeconomic status, working memory and worry
creator: Colton L. Hunter
description: Socioeconomic status is a complex psychological construct linked to a number of professional and personal barriers, including cognitive deficits. Current explanations of the link between socioeconomic status and cognition focus primarily on influences of external factors on development, with less attention paid to internal psychological mechanisms operating in the present.

title: Umfrage zur Versorgungssituation von Patient:innen mit systemischem Lupus erythematodes und systemischer Sklerose mit Lungenbeteiligung in Rheinland-Pfalz und dem Saarland
creator: Lennart Haßdenteufel, Kai Jahns, Ciaran Alberti, Andreas Schwarting, Matthias Dreher
description: HintergrundKollagenosen wie systemischer Lupus erythematodes (SLE) und systemische Sklerose (SSc) erfordern aufgrund multisystemischer Manifestationen eine interdisziplinäre Versorgung. Insbesondere die pulmonale Beteiligung (CTD-ILD) ist prognostisch relevant. Daten zur realen Versorgungssituation sind jedoch limitiert, wodurch strukturelle Defizite schwer identifizierbar bleiben.MethodikMit einem selbstentwickelten 14-moduligen Fragebogen wurden zwischen 09/2024 und 03/2025 insgesamt 2173 Praxen verschiedener Fachrichtungen in Rheinland-Pfalz und dem Saarland kontaktiert.

title: A longitudinal analysis of Clostridioides difficile virulence profiles across three geographic regions in Israel (2020–2022)
creator: Orna Schwartz, Avi Peretz, Maya Azrad
description: BackgroundClostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is one of the leading infectious diarrhea worldwide. C. difficile pathogenicity is mediated by various virulence factors, including toxins and biofilm formation. This study included 313 C. difficile isolates that were previously collected from four medical centers. We aimed to investigate the prevalence, distribution, and associations of virulence factors in C.

title: 黄芩清热除痹胶囊抑制类风湿关节炎成纤维样滑膜细胞炎症及增殖的机制
creator: 月迪 胡, 健 刘
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 目的明确烷基化修复同源蛋白5（ALKBH5）/环状RNA0091685（circ_0091685）/真核起始因子4A-Ⅲ（eIF4A3）轴在类风湿关节炎成纤维样滑膜细胞（RA-FLS）中的作用，并探讨黄芩清热除痹胶囊（HQC）是否通过该轴调控RA-FLS炎症及增殖。方法基于基因表达综合数据库（GEO）中的微阵列数据集筛选类风湿关节炎患者与健康人群的差异表达基因，并进行基因本体（GO）、京都基因和基因组数据库（KEGG）富集分析以筛选差异表达基因相关的生物学过程和作用通路。建立外周血单个核细胞和RA-FLS共培养模型，通过过表达或沉默ALKBH5、circ_0091685、EIF4A3，以及突变circ_0091685的N6-甲基腺苷（m6A）位点，验证ALKBH5是否通过介导circ_0091685 m6A修饰靶向eIF4A3影响RA-FLS炎症及增殖。同时建立佐剂性关节炎大鼠模型，观察HQC对大鼠的影响，并通过HQC含药血清作用于RA-FLS探索ALKBH5/circ_0091685/eIF4A3轴在HQC发挥疗效过程中的作用机制。在体外实验中，采用5-乙炔基-2 ´ -脱氧尿苷（EdU）染色检测细胞增殖能力、酶联免疫吸附试验检测炎症因子水平、逆转录定量聚合酶链反应检测EIF4A3和circ_0091685表达水平、蛋白质印迹法检测ALKBH5和eIF4A3表达水平、RNA免疫共沉淀法验证circ_0091685与eIF4A3结合、比色法及RNA甲基化免疫共沉淀-定量聚合酶链反应检测m6A修饰水平；在体内实验中，采用苏木精-伊红染色、番红O-固绿染色和甲苯胺蓝染色观察大鼠膝关节组织病理变化。结果GEO中，类风湿关节炎患者样本与健康人群样本的前20个差异表达基因包括ALKBH5和EIF4A3。GO分析显示生物学过程存在甲基化修饰，KEGG分析显示富集通路包括IL-17信号通路等。与ALKBH5沉默对照组比较，ALKBH5沉默组ALKBH5、circ_0091685、eIF4A3、IL-6、IL-17A、IL-23、TNF-α表达均减少，EdU相对阳性细胞数减少（均P<0.01），而ALKBH5过表达组则相反。与ALKBH5过表达+circ_0091685对照组比较，ALKBH5过表达+circ_0091685突变组炎症因子IL-6、IL-17A、IL-23、TNF-α表达均显著减少（均P<0.01）。RNA免疫共沉淀检测结果显示，circ_0091685可与eIF4A3特异性结合。沉默circ_0091685或EIF4A3均能降低细胞中炎症因子IL-6、IL-17A、IL-23、TNF-α表达水平，EdU相对阳性细胞数减少（均P<0.01），而过表达circ_0091685或EIF4A3则相反。HQC干预后，佐剂性关节炎大鼠膝关节组织病理有所改善。HQC含药血清干预后，RA-FLS中IL-6、IL-17A、IL-23、TNF-α、ALKBH5、circ_0091685、eIF4A3表达减少且EdU相对阳性细胞数减少（均P<0.05），而总RNA m6A和circ_0091685 m6A水平升高（均P<0.05）；在加入HQC含药血清基础上过表达ALKBH5能升高IL-6、IL-17A、IL-23、TNF-α表达水平（均P<0.01）；在加入HQC含药血清基础上过表达circ_0091685亦能升高IL-6、IL-23、TNF-α表达水平（均P<0.01）。此外，加入HQC含药血清或沉默circ_0091685均能降低IL-6、IL-23、TNF-α及eIF4A3表达（均P<0.01），表明HQC含药血清和沉默circ_0091685具有协同作用关系。结论HQC通过调控ALKBH5介导的circ_0091685 m6A修饰靶向eIF4A3抑制RA-FLS炎症及增殖。 RA是一种炎症性自身免疫病，可引起关节破坏，严重时可致关节畸形［1-2］。炎症刺激伴随RA发展全过程，慢性炎症刺激RA-FLS异常增殖、迁移，加速促炎性细胞因子分泌，加快骨侵袭和骨破坏［3-4］。RNA修饰是真核生物重要的转录后表观遗传修饰［5］。RNA的不同碱基上存在着约10种不同的甲基化标记，其中m6A是mRNA上最广泛的甲基化修饰［6］，ALKBH5是m6A修饰的关键去甲基化酶。研究显示，环状RNA m6A修饰参与肿瘤、胰腺炎、骨关节炎等多种炎症相关疾病的进展［7-10］，ALKBH5介导的去甲基化修饰显著影响RA的滑膜增生和侵袭［11］。本团队前期研究利用RA患者PBMC进行全转录组高通量测序检测了环状RNA表达谱，得到165个环状RNA，进一步通过生物信息学分析和RT-qPCR实验筛选获得了一个与RA免疫炎症相关且在RA患者中高表达的环状RNA——hsa_circ_0091685（以下简称circ_0091685）［12］。 健脾清热通络方的代表制剂HQC是安徽中医药大学第一附属医院的院内制剂，具有清热利湿、祛风止痛、健脾通络之功效。前期研究通过超高效液相色谱-串联质谱、指纹图谱对HQC的核心成分进行了鉴定，证明其核心成分黄芩苷、栀子苷、木犀草素、齐墩果酸、薏苡素、苦杏仁苷等含量较高、稳定性良好［13-14］。临床观察和动物实验证明HQC在缓解RA患者炎症反应和降低佐剂性关节炎大鼠炎症细胞、滑膜组织水肿中的作用［15-16］。然而，既往研究尚未从表观遗传修饰的角度探讨HQC抗炎和抗增殖的作用机制。本研究首先通过生物信息学筛选出ALKBH5和EIF4A3是RA的差异表达基因，初步探究其在m6A甲基化修饰中的作用。在此基础上，进一步结合体内外实验验证HQC通过ALKBH5介导circ_0091685 m6A修饰抑制RA-FLS炎症及增殖的机制，旨在为HQC临床应用于RA治疗提供科学依据。 材料与方法 数据来源及处理 在GEO中检索关键词“rheumatoid arthritis”、“homo sapiens”和“expression profiling by title: 脑脊液宏基因组学第二代测序在新生儿颅内感染诊断中的价值
creator: Lingchen LI, Lizhong DU, 方 余, 丽娜 刘
description: 目的探讨脑脊液宏基因组学第二代测序（mNGS）在新生儿颅内感染中的诊断性能及对临床决策的影响。方法采用回顾性观察性研究设计，纳入2020—2025年浙江大学医学院附属儿童医院收治的疑似颅内感染且进行脑脊液mNGS的新生儿。计算mNGS的敏感度及其与脑脊液培养-定量聚合酶链反应（qPCR）检测结果的一致性。基于预设标准评价其临床影响，将患儿标本分为有影响组和无影响组，探讨mNGS对临床决策产生积极影响的独立因素。结果61例疑诊颅内感染新生儿中48例确诊颅内感染，明确病原体者18例，其中9例仅由mNGS检出，占病原学诊断的50%。mNGS检出敏感度为31.3%（95%CI：18.7%~46.3%），高于脑脊液培养-qPCR检测的18.8%（95%CI：8.9%~32.6%），但差异无统计学意义（P=0.15）。mNGS与脑脊液培养-qPCR检测的阳性一致率为66.7%（95%CI：29.9%~92.5%），阴性一致率为76.9%（95%CI：60.7%~88.9%）。mNGS对23例患儿的临床决策产生了积极影响，包括12例阳性结果指导病原学诊断和治疗调整，和11例阴性结果指导抗感染降级或停止。多因素分析显示mNGS阳性是其产生积极影响的独立因素（OR=22.127，P<0.01）。结论脑脊液mNGS可在新生儿颅内感染的病原学诊断和临床决策上提供积极支持。Keywords: 颅内感染, 新生儿, 诊断, 脑脊液, 宏基因组学第二代测序, 回顾性研究 新生儿颅内感染是一种进展快、破坏性强的疾病，可导致严重的神经系统后遗症，患儿病死率高［1］。快速并准确地找到病原体有助于早期诊断和选择有效的抗感染药物，但新生儿颅内感染病原学诊断面临脑脊液标本量少、培养周期长、阳性率低、高质量循证检测手段有限等困境［1-3］。mNGS作为一种无偏倚测序核酸检测方法，具有敏感度高、检测快、检测范围广等优势，在病原学检测方面展现出较大潜力［4-6］。除病原学检测外，mNGS还可对耐药基因进行分析，为抗感染药物的选择提供依据。然而，由于mNGS费用高昂、临床诊断准确率不明确以及改善临床诊疗证据不充分［4-5］，mNGS尚未在临床实践中常规应用，在新生儿颅内感染中的研究报道更为有限。本研究回顾分析浙江大学医学院附属儿童医院收治的疑似颅内感染并进行脑脊液mNGS的新生儿资料，评估脑脊液mNGS在新生儿颅内感染诊断中的价值。 title: Visual analysis of [18F]FDG PET/CT imaging yields superior diagnostic accuracy compared to semiquantitative analysis in the assessment of giant cell arteritis
creator: Luca Seitz, Rahel Friedli, Nasir Gözlügöl, Susana Bucher, Pascal Seitz, Fabian Lötscher, Marc Gilgen, Jennifer Amsler, Patrick Stähli, Fabrice Helfenstein, Yvonne Döring, Györgyi Hamvas, Marc Schindewolf, Axel Rominger, Britta Maurer, Lisa Christ, Federico Caobelli
description: Background[¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT can be used to diagnose suspected new-onset giant cell arteritis (GCA), but it is unclear, whether visual or semiquantitative evaluation yields the highest accuracy. We therefore aimed to compare both methods with regard to diagnostic accuracy within the same patient.

title: The role of the family in youth psychiatric readmission: a scoping review
creator: Amos-Silvio Erik Friedrich, Magdalena Siegel, Joy Busch, Madlene Radosavljevic, Guy Bodenmann, Martina Zemp
description: Repeated admissions of children and adolescents after inpatient psychiatric treatment point to underrecognized issues in the post-discharge period. The family environment is a promising target for sustained recovery. However, recent systematic reviews on predictors of psychiatric readmission in children and adolescents were unable to synthesize most family-level factors due to conceptual and methodological differences.

title: Yahtzee: Reinforcement Learning Techniques for Stochastic Combinatorial Games
creator: Nicholas Pape
description: Abstract Yahtzee is a classic dice game with a stochastic, combinatorial structure and delayed rewards, making it an interesting mid-scale RL benchmark. While an optimal policy for solitaire Yahtzee can be computed using dynamic programming methods, multiplayer is intractable, motivating approximation methods.

title: Full grid solution for multi-asset options pricing with tensor networks
creator: Lucas Arenstein, Michael Kastoryano
description: Abstract Pricing multi-asset options via the Black–Scholes PDE is limited by the curse of dimensionality: classical full–grid solvers scale exponentially in the number of underlyings and are effectively restricted to three assets. Practitioners typically rely on Monte Carlo methods for computing complex instrument involving multiple correlated underlyings.

title: Neural Brain Fields: A NeRF-Inspired Approach for Generating Nonexistent EEG Electrodes
creator: Shahar Ain Kedem, Itamar Zimerman, Eliya Nachmani
description: Abstract Electroencephalography (EEG) data present unique modeling challenges because recordings vary in length, exhibit very low signal to noise ratios, differ significantly across participants, drift over time within sessions, and are rarely available in large and clean datasets. Consequently, developing deep learning methods that can effectively process EEG signals remains an open and important research problem.

Noé Stauffer: Laboratory for Computational Engineering, Empa, Dübendorf, Switzerland and CSQI Chair, École Polytec
creator: Noé Stauffer, Hossein Gorji and Ivan Lunati
description: Abstract . Model reduction techniques have emerged as a powerful paradigm across different fronts of scientific computing. Despite their success, the provided tools and methodologies remain limited if high-dimensional dynamical systems subject to initial uncertainty and/or stochastic noise are encountered; in particular if rare events are of interest.

title: The Physics of Olive Oil
creator: Sergey Parnovsky, A. A. Varlamov
description: Abstract Olive oil is an integral part of Mediterranean culture, shaped by more than three thousand years of history, rich traditions, evolving technologies, and fundamental physical principles. This article explores the role of physics in the production of olive oil, highlighting how physical laws govern each stage of the process.
